key_insight: In surgically repaired congenital heart disease, true gaps in follow-up care are common and are often driven by insurance instability and social vulnerability rather than medical necessity.
clinical_relevance: Patients who re-enter care after long gaps can present with significant disease progression and may need urgent intervention, with serious complications occurring across all CHD complexity levels.
method: Retrospective cohort of 1,746 patients with surgically repaired CHD at a tertiary center (2003–2020).
Combined electronic record screening with manual chart review to separate true gaps in care from appropriate follow-up patterns.
Defined gap in care as more than 3 years and 3 months between cardiology visits and beyond the recommended interval.
evidence_signal: From 916 potential gap cases, chart review refined this to 275 true gaps in care (15.7%), with multivariable analysis linking gaps to older age and simple CHD complexity.
watch_item: Single-center retrospective design and incomplete documentation of social contributors may limit how broadly these findings can be applied.
paper_title: Gaps in Congenital Heart Disease Care: Social Drivers and Clinical Consequences
